# Cassette — Idea Exploration (Round 4, recent)

## 1. Executive summary

The strongest signal across all 12 angles is that cassette's identity as "fixture AND governance object" is under-exploited on two fronts: (1) a snapshot-testing review lifecycle borrowed from insta/syrupy/ApprovalTests/Pact — pending sidecars, human-gated review, additive-only re-record, unreferenced pruning, and a can-i-deploy ship gate — which is the biggest DX and adoption gap and maps cleanly onto the existing opt-in record path; and (2) MCP as first-class LLM traffic, where the 2025-06-18 spec (sampling, elicitation, roots, OAuth, registry identity) opens net-new decoder-and-governance surface that only cassette's Transcript codec can serve offline. A third cluster — deterministic redteam detectors from garak/rebuff/mcp-scan (ANSI escapes, invisible-Unicode, canary leak, rug-pull, toxic-flow) — are small, pure-substring checks that slot into the existing exfil/taint/assert families with very high fit. Trace-interop (HAR/OTel import-export, W3C traceparent) turns dead capture corpora into replayable fixtures and makes cassette natively joinable to app traces without becoming a UI. Replay-debugger patterns from rr/Pernosco (reverse-step, event coordinates, dataflow origin tracing, offline near-miss diagnostics) deepen the inspect surface. The highest-leverage picks concentrate where effort is S/M and the feature is impossible without cassette's specific decoders. The clearest "do not do" traps re-tread rejected territory: anything requiring a live model, a hosted/stateful surface, or generic non-LLM VCR breadth.

## 2. How this was produced

A background workflow fanned out across 12 research angles (record/replay debuggers, snapshot testing, agent frameworks, the MCP ecosystem, AI red-team tooling, trace interop, local-first mocking, LLMOps awesome-lists, prompt versioning, provenance/supply-chain, CLI DX, and blue-sky). Each angle ran a web + GitHub search agent that extracted grounded idea candidates; every candidate was then adversarially vetted by an independent agent against cassette command surface, hard non-goals, and prior-round rejected list. Two completeness-critic passes searched for missing domains. Surviving ideas were deduped and clustered here.

Funnel: 97 candidates vetted -> 68 kept + 15 gap-added -> 83 distinct ideas.

## 3. Themes

### Review lifecycle & re-record safety

The single largest adoption/DX gap: a snapshot-tool-grade promotion workflow (pending sidecars, human-gated review, additive-only, batch collect) that keeps approved goldens immutable while letting a corpus grow safely on the opt-in record path.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| cassette review — human-gated accept/reject TUI for a re-recorded delta | M | 3 | 5 | [snapshot-testing](https://insta.rs/docs/cli/) | A new `review` command that operates ONLY on an explicit re-record delta (the opt-in `record`/`branch` network path already exists). Re-recording writes a `.pending` cassette next to the committed one rather than overwriting; `review` diffs committed-vs-pending per interaction in the terminal (reusing the existing `diff` SSE/Transcript decoder) and lets the operator accept/reject/skip each interaction, promoting only accepted ones. This is NOT auto self-healing (rejected): nothing is promoted without a human keystroke or an explicit `--accept` batch flag, and there is no live model in the replay path. Deterministic, offline, byte-exact promotion. |
| Additive-only re-record (new-only) — never mutate an approved interaction | M | 4 | 5 | [snapshot-testing](https://github.com/tophat/syrupy) | A `record --new-only` / `review --accept-unseen` mode: when re-recording against an existing cassette, brand-new interactions (a request shape with no prior match) are auto-added, but any interaction that would CHANGE an already-approved response is left as pending and must be reviewed manually. Lets teams grow a cassette to cover new prompts safely in CI-adjacent flows while guaranteeing approved goldens are immutable without a human accept. Opt-in network only during record; promotion is deterministic. |
| Pending-cassette sidecar convention (received vs approved) + JSON manifest for editors/CI | M | 3 | 5 | [snapshot-testing](https://github.com/approvals/ApprovalTests.cpp) | Formalize a `foo.cassette.yaml` (approved) + `foo.cassette.pending.yaml` (received) pair as the re-record artifact, and add `--as-json` output to the review/diff surface emitting a stable per-interaction manifest (interaction id, provider, old-hash, new-hash, decoded-diff) so an editor extension or a CI job can render the review without launching the TUI. CI can then hard-fail if any `.pending.yaml` is committed unresolved — a governance gate, no server, no network, purely file-and-hash based. |
| Batch collect-then-review: single 'replay --review' that gathers ALL drifts, then one accept/reject pass | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://insta.rs/docs/cli/) | The vetted list has the review TUI and pending sidecar as separate pieces, but not the workflow verb that ties them: a single command that runs a full replay pass in a non-failing collect mode, accumulates every drifted interaction into pendings in one shot, then hands the whole batch to review — plus non-interactive accept-all / reject-all for scripted use and a skip-and-keep-pending for partial sessions. This is the ergonomic spine cargo-insta users expect; it turns N re-record round-trips into one collect + one review. |
| Unreferenced-interaction lifecycle: warn / reject / delete / auto(CI-aware) | M | 3 | 4 | [snapshot-testing](https://insta.rs/docs/cli/) | Add an `--unreferenced=ignore/warn/reject/delete/auto` policy to the review/re-record surface: after a replay or re-record run, interactions in the cassette that were never matched get flagged. `auto` rejects in CI (dead fixtures are a governance smell) but offers to prune them locally. Pruning is deterministic and only touches interactions provably unhit by the run's dial log; it never contacts the network. This makes cassettes self-cleaning against drift without any self-healing re-record (rejected) — it only ever DELETES stale entries, never fabricates new ones. |
| Pending/WIP semantics: new cassettes join non-blocking until promoted | S | 3 | 4 | [local-mocking](https://docs.pact.io/pact_broker/can_i_deploy) | A 'pending' governance flag in a cassette's header: pending cassettes are still replayed and reported in `verify`/`assert` output but do NOT contribute to the CI failure gate until an explicit `cassette promote` clears the flag. This gives teams a safe way to land new recorded scenarios that aren't yet trusted (freshly recorded, not reviewed) without either blocking the pipeline or leaving them untracked — a purely static header field cassette's existing gating commands already read. Deterministic, offline, and reinforces the cassette-as-governance-object identity. |

### MCP 2025-06-18 spec surface as governed LLM traffic

The new MCP spec adds nested LLM calls (sampling), structured prompts (elicitation), scope boundaries (roots), auth secrets (OAuth), and identity (registry) — all currently invisible fixture/governance surface that cassette's decoders can uniquely capture and check offline.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| Record and govern MCP sampling (server-initiated createMessage) as nested LLM traffic | L | 4 | 5 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/client/sampling) | Extend the mcp-serve/mcp-proxy stdio decoder to recognize sampling/createMessage requests and their results as first-class LLM turns, folding their messages/content into the same Transcript codec used for Anthropic/OpenAI HTTP traffic. On replay, cassette answers the server's sampling request byte-exact from the stored result (the stored completion IS the fixture judge) with zero egress — letting agentic MCP servers be tested offline. Deterministic, no live model, reuses the existing Transcript decoder moat. |
| Record/replay MCP elicitation prompts and assert the requested JSON Schema | L | 4 | 5 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/client/elicitation) | Teach the MCP decoder to capture elicitation/create requests and their accept/decline/cancel responses so a recorded session can be replayed deterministically (the stored user answer is supplied automatically, keeping replay hands-off and zero-egress). Then add an elicitation lint to the existing schema-check/lint path: flag any recorded requestedSchema whose property titles/descriptions match sensitive-field patterns (password, ssn, card, secret) — a spec-conformance governance check over stored bytes, no network, no ML. |
| Roots-boundary audit: detect MCP server access outside declared filesystem roots | M | 4 | 4 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/client/roots) | cassette records the roots/list response (the declared boundary set) alongside every subsequent tool call in the same session. Add a boundary lens to the existing egress-audit family: parse file:// and path-shaped arguments/results out of recorded MCP calls and flag any that escape the declared roots (path traversal, absolute paths outside the set, symlink-looking segments). This is deterministic path arithmetic over already-recorded bytes; complements the existing network egress counter with a filesystem-scope counter. |
| OAuth/Bearer redaction profile for MCP streamable-HTTP transport | M | 4 | 4 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/basic/authorization) | Ship a built-in MCP-OAuth redaction profile for the existing redact-field/redact path: a named, deterministic ruleset that scrubs Authorization bearer values, refresh_token, code, code_verifier/challenge, state, and client_secret from recorded MCP streamable-HTTP cassettes, while preserving the non-sensitive resource audience URI so audience-mismatch (confused-deputy) can still be asserted. Static rules, no classifier, keeps fixtures shareable and byte-exact. |
| Provenance stamp from the official registry: bind a cassette to a namespaced server.json identity | M | 4 | 4 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/registry) | Extend the existing provenance command so an MCP cassette can carry the recorded server's registry identity (namespace + version + the server.json it presented at record time) as governance metadata. On later inspection, cassette flags when a replayed/re-recorded session's advertised tool set no longer matches the server.json version it was recorded against — an offline authenticity/version-drift check. Reads a checked-in server.json snapshot (fetched at record time only), never at replay; no live network on the default path. |
| MCP wire-conformance handshake checks (JSON-RPC 2.0 + spec-version negotiation) baked into the recorder | M | 3 | 4 | [llmops-awesome](https://github.com/studiomeyer-io/mcp-protocol-conformance) | cassette already has a 'conformance' verb, but it can be sharpened for MCP specifically at RECORD time: when mcp-serve/mcp-proxy captures a stdio session, statically validate the recorded frames for JSON-RPC 2.0 well-formedness (id/method/params/result/error shape), detect which MCP spec-version was negotiated in the initialize handshake, and stamp that version + any wire violations into the cassette metadata. Then a stored cassette carries a provable 'recorded against MCP 2025-06-18, JSON-RPC clean' attestation that verify-attest can later check offline. This is deterministic frame validation over already-captured bytes (no live server needed on replay), and it deepens the MCP decoder moat rather than duplicating the generic conformance verb. |

### Deterministic redteam detectors over recorded bytes

garak/rebuff/mcp-scan/mcp-gateway all ship pure-pattern (no-ML) detectors. Cassette already stores byte-exact output, so these become offline, reproducible governance checks in the exfil/taint/assert families — mostly small effort, very high fit.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| ANSI terminal-escape injection scanner over recorded model output | S | 3 | 5 | [ai-redteam](https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak/blob/main/garak/detectors/ansiescape.py) | A deterministic detector inside the existing `exfil`/`taint` family (or a new sub-check surfaced through `audit`) that walks the decoded Transcript assistant-text and tool-result fields of a recorded cassette and flags any ANSI/OSC escape byte sequences, reporting exact byte offset + event index. Because cassette stores byte-exact SSE/MCP output already, this runs entirely offline over recorded bytes with zero egress and fully reproducible output — the escape table is a vendored constant, no classifier. |
| Invisible-Unicode / tag-smuggling detector for recorded prompts and completions | S | 3 | 5 | [ai-redteam](https://github.com/protectai/llm-guard) | Add an offline codepoint-class scan to `redact-field`/`taint`: for a recorded cassette, flag (and optionally, in a transform command, strip) invisible/zero-width/bidi/tag-block Unicode in both request messages and stored completions, emitting a governance finding with codepoint + offset. Deterministic Unicode-table lookup over already-recorded bytes; respects zero-egress and no-classifier non-goals. Fits the 'cassette is a governance object' framing. |
| Known-bad test-signature assertion (EICAR / GTUBE / GTphish) as a stored-fixture policy check | S | 3 | 5 | [ai-redteam](https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak/blob/main/garak/detectors/knownbadsignatures.py) | Extend the existing `assert`/`expect` grammar with a built-in deterministic signature set (EICAR/GTUBE/GTphish plus custom substrings) so a recorded cassette can assert 'the model's stored completion must NOT contain signature X' or, for negative-control fixtures, 'must contain it.' This turns a cassette into a regression fixture for output-safety controls — a pure substring assertion over recorded bytes, no live call. |
| Canary-token leak detection: prove a system prompt / secret did not surface in recorded output | S | 2 | 5 | [ai-redteam](https://github.com/protectai/rebuff) | A `verify`-style check that, given a canary string known to live only in the system prompt / injected context of a recorded cassette, deterministically searches every stored completion and tool-result for that literal token and fails if it leaked. Because cassette already holds the full request (system prompt) and byte-exact response, leak-detection is a within-fixture substring comparison — fully offline, reproducible, and it directly operationalizes OWASP LLM07 over recorded traffic. |
| Rug-pull tripwire: pin tool descriptions/schemas by hash across cassettes | S | 2 | 5 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://github.com/invariantlabs-ai/mcp-scan) | A cassette already records the full MCP initialize/tools-list handshake for a stdio session. Add an assertion mode to the existing verify/assert path that, given TWO cassettes (or a cassette plus a checked-in baseline manifest), computes a stable content hash per (server,tool) over name+description+inputSchema and flags any drift as a rug-pull finding. This is pure offline diffing over already-stored fixture bytes — no live network, no LLM classifier, deterministic. The cassette IS the pinned baseline (governance object), so this needs no external DB. |
| Tool-description hidden-instruction lint (poisoning signatures) for recorded tool lists | M | 4 | 5 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://github.com/lasso-security/mcp-gateway) | Add a poisoning-signature ruleset to the existing lint/exfil path that runs over the tool descriptions already captured in an MCP cassette's tools/list: flag imperative-to-the-model phrasing ('ignore previous', 'do not tell the user', 'read ~/.ssh', hidden HTML/comment blocks, unicode-tag smuggling). The ruleset is a checked-in, versioned pattern fixture — deterministic, offline, no LLM classifier — turning the cassette into a static poisoning-audit artifact for CI. |
| Static MCP tool-definition risk scan over the recorded MCP handshake | M | 4 | 5 | [ai-redteam](https://github.com/splx-ai/agentic-radar) | Cassette's MCP capture already records the initialize/tools-list handshake byte-exact. Add a deterministic static lint (extending `mcp-steps`/`lint`) that inspects the recorded tool schemas for risk signals — tools whose descriptions request secrets/exfiltrate, overly broad/`any` argument schemas, shell/exec/file-write capabilities (Excessive Agency, LLM06), or tool-description text containing hidden instructions/invisible Unicode. It's a rule set over the recorded tool manifest: offline, no agent execution, deterministic, and it makes a stored MCP cassette a reviewable governance object. |
| Toxic-flow / cross-server data-exfil path detection over a recorded MCP session | M | 3 | 4 | [mcp-ecosystem](https://github.com/lasso-security/mcp-gateway) | cassette's mcp-steps already reconstructs the ordered call sequence of a recorded stdio session. Add a taint/data-flow lens (extends the existing taint command from HTTP to MCP): mark tool RESULTS from untrusted/read-heavy servers as tainted, then flag any later tool CALL whose arguments contain a substring derived from a tainted result AND that targets a sink tool matched by a stored, user-editable sink pattern list (exec/write/send/http). Fully deterministic string-provenance over recorded bytes; the sink list is a checked-in fixture, not an ML model. |

### Trace & capture-format interop

Bridges dead artifacts (HAR dumps, OTel span exports) into replayable cassettes and stamps W3C traceparent so cassette exports join the app's own traces — all pure offline serialization over bytes cassette already owns, never a UI.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| export har: emit a byte-exact HAR 1.2 file from a recorded cassette | S | 3 | 5 | [trace-interop](http://www.softwareishard.com/blog/har-12-spec/) | A new `export har` transform that walks the stored interactions and writes a deterministic HAR 1.2 log (stable entry ordering, canonical header casing preserved, SSE responses folded into content.text with mimeType text/event-stream, base64 for binary). Pure offline serialization of bytes cassette already owns; no network, no new decoder. Lets users open a cassette in browser devtools / Charles / any HAR viewer without cassette ever becoming a trace UI. Round-trips with a matching `import har` (below) so an existing HAR corpus of LLM traffic becomes replayable fixtures. |
| import har: ingest an existing HAR capture into a replayable cassette | M | 4 | 4 | [trace-interop](http://www.softwareishard.com/blog/har-12-spec/) | A `port`-family / `import har` transform that filters HAR entries to known provider hosts (reuse the existing provider host matchers), rebuilds each request+response, and feeds the response body through cassette's existing Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama/Cohere decoders to produce a byte-exact replayable cassette. Deterministic, offline, no live network. This is NOT a generic non-LLM VCR: the value-add is that only LLM-shaped entries are lifted and the provider Transcript codec is applied — a HAR file alone can't replay SSE semantics. |
| Multi-format artifact import: seed a cassette skeleton from an OpenAPI/HAR file | M | 4 | 4 | [local-mocking](https://microcks.io/documentation/references/artifacts/) | A `cassette import --har` path that reads a browser/proxy-captured HTTP Archive (HAR) of an LLM session and converts the matching provider requests/responses into a cassette skeleton (canonicalized, with SSE reassembled where the HAR captured chunked bodies). This lets teams who already captured traffic via devtools/Charles/mitmproxy bootstrap a cassette without re-running the live calls through cassette's proxy — a one-shot offline file transform (HAR in, cassette YAML out), no live network, reusing cassette's existing provider decoders to interpret the bodies. Distinct from existing `port`/`migrate` which move between cassette formats; this ingests a foreign capture format. |
| import otel-genai: lift a captured OTLP/JSON GenAI span dump into a replay cassette | L | 4 | 4 | [trace-interop](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/main/docs/gen-ai/README.md) | An `import otel-genai` transform that reads OTLP/JSON spans, and for spans whose gen_ai.provider.name is a supported provider, reconstructs a synthetic-but-byte-plausible request/response pair (re-encoding messages into that provider's wire shape via the existing internal/wireenc) to yield a replayable cassette. Deterministic, offline. Distinct from the rejected 'LLM fixture generator': nothing is generated by a model — the messages come verbatim from the captured span, cassette only re-frames known content into the provider's transport format so it can be replayed and governed. |
| trace-context binding: honor and stamp W3C traceparent on record/replay | S | 4 | 4 | [trace-interop](https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context/) | Capture the inbound traceparent/tracestate as first-class per-interaction metadata during record, and (opt-in) on replay echo a deterministic traceparent derived from the interaction's stable hash so the replayed call correlates in the caller's tracer. This also gives the OpenInference/OTel/Chrome exporters above a real trace_id/span_id to populate instead of synthesizing one, making cassette exports natively joinable to the app's own traces. Metadata capture only — no live tracing backend, no network egress on replay beyond the header cassette already returns. |

### Replay debugging & mismatch diagnostics

rr/Pernosco/WireMock/diffoscope patterns: reverse-step, stable event coordinates, dataflow origin tracing, ranked near-miss diagnostics, and recursive decode-layer diffing — all deterministic functions over stored bytes that deepen inspect/diff/explain.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| Reverse-step / rewind over the stored event timeline | M | 4 | 5 | [replay-debuggers](https://pernos.co/about/overview/) | Add a deterministic step-cursor mode to an existing look/inspect command that walks the SSE/MCP event timeline both forward AND backward (prev/next event), reconstructing the exact accumulated response text or tool-call state at each stop purely from stored bytes. Because a cassette is a fully-recorded deterministic artifact, 'rewind' is just re-seeking the codec to an earlier event coordinate — no live model, no network, no nondeterminism. This is the offline analog of reverse-continue, not the timing/waterfall views already rejected. |
| Stable event-coordinate addressing + "goto event N" replay seek | M | 3 | 4 | [replay-debuggers](https://github.com/rr-debugger/rr/wiki/Usage) | Define a canonical, byte-exact event coordinate that unifies HTTP request index + SSE chunk ordinal + MCP step ordinal into one address (e.g. `iX/sseY` or `mcp:stepZ`), computed deterministically from the stored cassette. Add a `--at <coord>` flag to the existing inspect/diff/explain read commands so they can pin to one event, and a replay seek that stops emission exactly at that coordinate. This is an addressing scheme over already-stored bytes (no new capture, no network, fully deterministic) and is finer-grained than mcp-steps, which only enumerates MCP calls. |
| Intra-transcript field origin tracing (where did this output byte come from?) | L | 4 | 4 | [replay-debuggers](https://pernos.co/about/overview/) | Given a location in the decoded/assembled response (e.g. a character range in the final assistant message, or a JSON field in a reconstructed tool-call args object), trace it deterministically back to the exact wire event(s) that produced it — which SSE delta frame(s), which MCP step, which byte offset. This is a decode-provenance query internal to ONE transcript (distinct from the existing `provenance` command about cassette lineage/attestation, and distinct from `taint` which tracks cross-cassette contamination). Pure function over stored bytes via the existing SSE/MCP decoders; no ML, no network. |
| Distance-ranked replay-miss diagnostics ('did you mean this interaction?') | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://wiremock.org/docs/verifying/) | When replay fails to find a matching stored interaction, instead of a bare miss, cassette emits a deterministic ranked list of the N closest stored interactions and a field-level diff of the mismatch (which normalized/matched field diverged: model, tool name, prompt hash, header). This is a pure offline computation over the stored Transcript + the in-cassette matcher policy already on the vetted list, so no network and no nondeterminism. It converts the single hardest DX moment (a silent/cryptic replay miss) into an actionable diff. Distinct from existing diff (which compares two cassettes) — this diagnoses a live request against the corpus. |
| diffoscope-style recursive root-cause explainer for replay mismatches | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:governance-moat-and-novel-use-cases](https://github.com/anthraxx/diffoscope) | When a replay assertion fails, cassette can recursively decode both sides through the SAME provider decoders it already owns (SSE frames -> Transcript events -> nested JSON tool-args -> base64/gzip payloads) and report the mismatch at the deepest decoded layer with a category tag (volatile-timestamp, reordered-set, re-encoded-number, added-field), instead of a top-level byte diff. This is the LLM-wire-aware analog of diffoscope and leans on decoders that only cassette has. Fully offline and deterministic. |
| onUnmatched strictness policy: bypass / warn / error for incoming replay requests | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://mswjs.io/docs/api/setup-server/) | A first-class replay-strictness knob on serve/mcp-serve (and honored in cassette headers) that governs what happens when an incoming request matches no stored interaction: strict (fail with the near-miss diagnostic), warn (log and return a canned deterministic stub), or reject-with-empty. This is orthogonal to the already-vetted unreferenced-interaction lifecycle (which governs stored records nobody hit) — this governs live requests nobody stored. Stays zero-egress: 'bypass' here means canned-response, never a real network call. |
| Live-replay coverage manifest: which stored interactions fired vs never hit this run | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://wiremock.org/docs/stubbing/) | A per-run (not per-corpus) manifest emitted by serve/mcp-serve on shutdown: for THIS replay session, which stored interactions were exercised, which were never hit, and which incoming requests missed. The existing coverage command is a static analysis of the cassette; this is dynamic, tied to one server lifetime, and directly feeds the unreferenced-lifecycle pruning already on the list. Deterministic (just an atomic hit-counter per interaction, mirroring the existing dial counter), zero-egress. |

### Declarative content & behavioral contracts

Move governance beyond byte-equality: named deterministic content checks (PCSL), cross-provider ordering assertions, MCP trajectory match modes, provider-state preconditions, and a self-describing normalize/matcher block — all stored in the YAML as travelling contract.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| PCSL-style layered output contract stored inside the cassette (structural / semantic checks, deterministic tier only) | M | 3 | 5 | [llmops-awesome](https://github.com/philippmelikidis/prompt-contracts) | cassette already has assert/expect/verify but they operate largely on transcript-level equality. Borrow PCSL's decomposition into named, declarative, deterministic content checks that live in the cassette YAML and travel with it as part of the governance object: a small library of pure-Go checkers (json-parses, required-fields-present, JSONPath-value-in-enum, regex-absent, token/word budget) attached to a decoded response body. Because a cassette is both fixture and governance object, these become a self-describing 'expectation suite' that any consumer of the cassette can re-verify offline with zero egress — no LLM judge, no network. This is distinct from the shipped verbs because it standardizes a reusable, named check vocabulary on the DECODED semantic body (not byte diff), grounded in JSONPath/regex, which is the LLM-response-shape moat rather than generic HTTP assertions. |
| Cross-format cassette content assertions (verify-contains / verify-ordering over the Transcript) | S | 2 | 5 | [agent-frameworks](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/tests/cassette_utils.py) | Extend the existing `assert`/`expect` command family with an ordering-aware matcher that operates on the decoded Transcript rather than raw bytes: `cassette assert --contains 'tool:search' --contains 'text:refusal'` and `cassette assert --order 'tool:get_weather < text:sunny'`. Because cassette already normalizes every provider (Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama/Cohere) into one Transcript codec, this gives the single cross-provider assertion surface pydantic-ai had to hand-roll per provider — deterministic, offline, byte-source-of-truth, no new network path. |
| Trajectory match modes for MCP replay assertions (strict / unordered / subset / superset) | M | 2 | 5 | [llmops-awesome](https://github.com/langchain-ai/agentevals) | cassette's existing mcp-diff/mcp-steps and assert/expect treat a recorded MCP transcript as a single canonical sequence. Add a match-mode dimension to the assert/expect verbs (or a new stored assertion block in the cassette YAML) so a cassette can encode intent: 'these two tools must fire in order', 'this tool must never be called (forbidden)', 'these tools may fire in any order', 'no tools beyond this allowlist'. Plus per-tool argument matchers (exact / ignore / required-fields / numeric-tolerance) stored declaratively in the YAML. This stays 100% deterministic and offline — it is comparison logic over the already-decoded MCP tool-call stream, no live model, no classifier. It upgrades the governance object from 'byte-exact or bust' to 'byte-exact wire replay PLUS a declared behavioral contract on the tool-call shape', which is exactly the LLM/MCP-specific moat and not a generic VCR feature. |
| Provider-state preconditions block for stateful MCP replay sequences | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://docs.pact.io/getting_started/how_pact_works) | An optional named-precondition tag on MCP interactions in the cassette: each tool-call/resource interaction can declare the state it assumes (e.g. 'file X written', 'session authenticated'), and replay asserts those states hold from prior interactions in the same session rather than relying on raw positional order. Complements the vetted trajectory match modes (strict/unordered/subset) by giving the unordered/subset modes a declarative dependency graph. Pure metadata in the YAML, checked offline. |
| In-cassette normalization/matcher policy block (regex + typed placeholders) governing volatile fields | S | 2 | 5 | [snapshot-testing](https://insta.rs/docs/filters/) | A declarative `normalize:` policy block stored inside the cassette YAML itself (the file is already 'fixture AND governance object'): an ordered list of regex->placeholder rules applied to raw SSE/text bodies, plus JSON-path typed matchers (`is: uuid/iso8601/number`) applied to structured request/response fields. Applied deterministically at both record-normalize time and replay-match time so a volatile `request_id`/timestamp matches by type rather than byte-equality. This generalizes the existing single-field `redact-field` into a governed, self-describing matcher set. No LLM classifier (rejected) — rules are explicit regex/JSON-path, fully deterministic. |

### Prompt versioning & drift gates

MLflow/Langfuse-style immutable prompt versioning maps to hash-pinned drift gates, structural prompt diffs, and prompt-lineage facets in the existing offline HTML browser — deterministic, offline, no model.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| Prompt-version drift gate: assert the wire prompt matches a pinned content hash | S | 3 | 5 | [prompt-versioning](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started) | Add a policy sub-check (a stored assertion, not a new top-level command — it slots under `policy`/`assert` semantics) that computes the canonicalized hash of the outbound prompt/system/tool-definition bytes in a cassette and compares it to a pinned expected hash committed alongside. On mismatch it fails in CI, so an accidental prompt edit that would change model behavior is caught deterministically offline before anyone re-records. Pure byte comparison, zero egress, no model in the loop. |
| Cross-version prompt diff with variant-aware highlighting | M | 3 | 5 | [prompt-versioning](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/genai/prompt-registry/) | Teach the existing `diff` command a prompt-aware mode that, given two cassettes, diffs the decoded outbound prompt structure (system block, tool definitions, few-shot demos, user turn) region-by-region rather than raw-byte, so a reviewer sees exactly which part of the prompt changed between two recorded versions. Deterministic structural diff over provider-decoded bytes; reuses cassette's per-provider decoders (the actual moat). |
| Cross-cassette prompt lineage view: which fixtures share the same prompt | M | 4 | 4 | [prompt-versioning](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started) | Extend the existing `coverage`/`dashboard` offline HTML output (already shipped via `pack`) to group cassettes by the content-hash of their outbound prompt, so a corpus browser shows 'these 14 fixtures all exercise prompt <sha>, these 3 diverge'. This is a read-only offline index over already-recorded bytes — no live network, no stateful server, just an additional facet in the self-contained HTML browser. |
| Consumer-impact breaking-change classifier for a re-recorded cassette (semver-style) | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:governance-moat-and-novel-use-cases](https://github.com/oasdiff/oasdiff) | cassette diff today shows what changed byte-for-byte; it does not tell you whether a delta would break a REPLAY CONSUMER. Add a classification layer over the existing Transcript diff: a removed tool, a narrowed JSON-Schema, or a dropped SSE event type is 'breaking' (a replaying client's assertions will now fail); an added optional field or a new any-of variant is 'compatible'. Emit a recommended cassette-version bump (major/minor/patch) and a nonzero exit code on breaking deltas so CI can gate re-records. Purely deterministic over stored bytes, no network, no model. |
| Policy/matcher pack breaking-change gate across cassette-schema versions | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:governance-moat-and-novel-use-cases](https://buf.build/docs/breaking/overview) | cassette's in-cassette normalization/matcher policy block and policy packs are themselves shared contracts that many fixtures depend on. Add a check that compares a proposed matcher/policy-pack version against the prior one and flags edits that would retroactively change whether EXISTING cassettes pass (e.g. tightening a placeholder regex, removing a tolerance matcher). Prevents a policy edit from silently invalidating or silently rubber-stamping an approved corpus. Deterministic, offline, evaluated over the stored corpus. |

### Provenance, attestation & self-validating packs

Strengthen the governance moat: sealed self-contained bundles, transparency-log inclusion proofs, machine-readable DataCards, policy-pack unit tests + coverage, reproducibility-witness double-capture, and a can-i-deploy ship gate.

| Idea | Effort | Nov | Fit | Source | How it maps to cassette |
|------|--------|-----|-----|--------|-------------------------|
| Portable self-contained recording bundle (rr pack analog for external refs) | M | 4 | 4 | [replay-debuggers](https://github.com/rr-debugger/rr/wiki/Usage) | Extend the existing `pack` beyond the offline HTML browser: add a 'seal' mode that resolves and inlines every external reference a cassette leans on for deterministic replay (referenced judge fixtures, split/merge parents, external schema files for schema-check, redaction rulesets) into one self-verifying bundle, so replay+verify is reproducible on a fresh machine with nothing else present. Mirrors rr pack's 'remove dependencies elsewhere on the system' guarantee; stays offline and byte-exact. |
| Offline-verifiable transparency-log inclusion proof bundled into the attestation | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:governance-moat-and-novel-use-cases](https://github.com/sigstore/rekor) | The vetted list has DSSE/cosign SIGNING of the attestation but nothing that proves WHEN and that it was publicly witnessed. Extend the attestation-signing feature to optionally embed a transparency-log inclusion proof (Rekor-compatible) so `cassette verify-attest` can confirm, fully offline from the bundled proof, that the cassette attestation was logged and cannot be silently backdated. Only the one-time proof fetch touches the network (opt-in, like record); verification stays zero-egress. Strengthens the governance/non-repudiation moat. |
| Machine-readable cassette DataCard (Croissant-style) with license + provenance fields | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:governance-moat-and-novel-use-cases](https://github.com/mlcommons/croissant) | A cassette is a dataset (recorded LLM/MCP interactions) but carries no standardized, machine-readable statement of WHERE the recording came from, under what license/ToS the captured provider content may be used, or its intended-use restrictions. Add a governed DataCard block (or emit a Croissant-flavored JSON export) capturing provider, capture date, license/ToS assertion, PII/redaction status, and intended-use scope. A `cassette policy check` rule can then refuse to replay a fixture in a context that violates its declared intended use. Static metadata, deterministic, no network. |
| conftest-style policy unit tests + rule coverage for cassette policy packs | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:governance-moat-and-novel-use-cases](https://github.com/open-policy-agent/conftest) | cassette already has ~a dozen policy/govern commands but no way to TEST the policies themselves. Add a `cassette policy verify` convention: a policy pack ships alongside fixture cassettes that are expected-pass and expected-fail, plus assertions, and cassette runs the policy over them and reports per-rule pass/fail AND rule coverage (which policy clauses no policy-test ever triggered). This makes a policy pack self-validating and catches dead/over-broad rules before distribution. Deterministic, offline, reuses existing policy engine. |
| Reproducibility-witness co-record: independent double-capture that must agree modulo declared volatility | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:governance-moat-and-novel-use-cases](https://reproducible-builds.org/tools/) | Offer a `record --witness` mode that captures the same request twice (or ingests a second independently-recorded capture) and asserts the two agree AFTER applying the cassette's own normalization/matcher policy block — flagging any field that varied but was NOT declared volatile. This turns 'is this provider response actually deterministic / did I redact everything nondeterministic?' into a provable, deterministic check, and hardens the matcher policy against under-declared volatile fields. Network only during the opt-in record step. |
| can-i-deploy safety gate: query whether a consumer + its pinned cassettes are compatible before shipping | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://docs.pact.io/getting_started/how_pact_works) | A CI-facing verb that answers, offline: 'given this app version pins cassette set S at hashes H, is every referenced interaction present, unexpired (per the reproducibility env-lock header already vetted), and passing its stored policy pack?' It aggregates the results of verify/attest/policy into one deploy/no-deploy exit code + machine-readable matrix, without any broker or network — the cassettes and their signed attestations ARE the offline compatibility matrix. Fills the 'is it safe to ship against these fixtures' gap the current per-command checks leave to the user to assemble. |
| Cassette-as-contract validation proxy: assert opt-in recorded traffic conforms before it is stored | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://github.com/stoplightio/prism) | During the opt-in record/branch path (the only place cassette touches the network), run the captured request/response pairs through the cassette's own stored matcher policy + schema-check + conformance rules AS they are captured, and reject/flag interactions that violate the cassette's declared contract before they are committed. This makes record a governed gate rather than a raw dump — a provider-verification analog that reuses the existing conformance/schema-check machinery, and only ever runs where network is already permitted. |
| Declarative .tape script to regenerate a cassette-driven terminal demo deterministically | M | 4 | 4 | [gap:adoption-and-DX](https://github.com/charmbracelet/vhs) | A 'cassette demo' emitter that, given a cassette, generates a deterministic scripted tape (the recorded interactions replayed at fixed pacing against the offline binary) that regenerates the per-feature explainer recordings the repo already ships — so docs GIFs are rebuilt from the fixture + a checked-in script instead of manually captured. Since replay is already byte-exact and zero-egress, the produced demo is fully reproducible in offline CI. Pure DX for the docs pipeline; no runtime feature and no non-Go dependency required in the binary itself (tape is an output artifact). |

## 4. Top recommendations (ranked by leverage)

1. **cassette review — human-gated accept/reject TUI for a re-recorded delta** — insta-style pending-then-promote review over a re-record delta, reusing the diff decoders. _(effort M, leverage very high)_ [source](https://insta.rs/docs/cli/)
   - Re-record writes a .pending cassette beside the committed one; review diffs committed-vs-pending per interaction via the existing SSE/Transcript diff decoder and promotes only accepted ones. Nothing promotes without a human keystroke or explicit --accept, so it is not the rejected self-healing re-record.
2. **Record and govern MCP sampling (server-initiated createMessage) as nested LLM traffic** — Fold server-initiated sampling/createMessage LLM calls into the Transcript codec for offline replay. _(effort L, leverage very high)_ [source](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-06-18/client/sampling)
   - Extend the mcp-serve/mcp-proxy stdio decoder to recognize sampling/createMessage requests+results as first-class LLM turns using the same Transcript codec as HTTP providers; replay answers the server's sampling request byte-exact with zero egress. This is exactly the LLM traffic cassette specializes in, currently invisible on the stdio channel.
3. **Distance-ranked replay-miss diagnostics ('did you mean this interaction?')** — Turn a cryptic replay miss into a ranked near-miss list with field-level mismatch breakdown. _(effort M, leverage very high)_ [source](https://wiremock.org/docs/verifying/)
   - On a replay match failure, compute a deterministic normalized distance against every stored interaction (model, tool name, prompt hash, headers) and surface the top N closest with which field diverged. Pure offline computation over the stored Transcript plus the in-cassette matcher policy; fixes the single hardest DX moment.
4. **Cross-format cassette content assertions (verify-contains / verify-ordering over the Transcript)** — One cross-provider ordering-aware assertion surface over the decoded Transcript. _(effort S, leverage high)_ [source](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-ai/blob/main/tests/cassette_utils.py)
   - Extend assert/expect with matchers on the decoded Transcript rather than raw bytes: --contains 'tool:search' and --order 'tool:get_weather < text:sunny'. Because every provider normalizes to one Transcript codec, this delivers the single assertion surface pydantic-ai had to hand-roll per provider.
5. **ANSI terminal-escape injection scanner over recorded model output** — Deterministic garak-style ANSI/OSC escape detector over decoded output, reporting byte offsets. _(effort S, leverage high)_ [source](https://github.com/NVIDIA/garak/blob/main/garak/detectors/ansiescape.py)
   - Walk decoded Transcript assistant-text and tool-result fields for ANSI/OSC control sequences using a vendored escape table, reporting event index and byte offset. Runs entirely offline over bytes cassette already stores, no classifier; slots into exfil/audit.
6. **Canary-token leak detection: prove a system prompt / secret did not surface in recorded output** — Rebuff-style substring proof that a system-prompt canary never leaked into any completion. _(effort S, leverage high)_ [source](https://github.com/protectai/rebuff)
   - Given a canary token known to live only in the system prompt/injected context, deterministically search every stored completion and tool-result for that literal and fail on leak. Within-fixture substring comparison operationalizing OWASP LLM07 fully offline.
7. **import har: ingest an existing HAR capture into a replayable cassette** — Lift LLM-shaped HAR entries into byte-exact replayable cassettes via existing provider decoders. _(effort M, leverage high)_ [source](http://www.softwareishard.com/blog/har-12-spec/)
   - Filter HAR entries to known provider hosts (reuse existing host matchers), rebuild request+response, and feed bodies through the Anthropic/OpenAI/Gemini/Ollama/Cohere decoders. Not a generic VCR: only LLM-shaped entries are lifted and the provider Transcript codec is applied so SSE semantics replay.
8. **export har: emit a byte-exact HAR 1.2 file from a recorded cassette** — Serialize stored interactions to HAR 1.2 so any devtools/Charles/mitmproxy viewer opens a cassette. _(effort S, leverage high)_ [source](http://www.softwareishard.com/blog/har-12-spec/)
   - Walk stored interactions into a deterministic HAR log with stable ordering, preserved header casing, and SSE folded into content.text as text/event-stream. Pure offline serialization of bytes cassette already owns; cassette never becomes a trace UI.
9. **Rug-pull tripwire: pin tool descriptions/schemas by hash across cassettes** — Hash-pin (server,tool) name+description+inputSchema and flag silent drift between cassettes. _(effort S, leverage high)_ [source](https://github.com/invariantlabs-ai/mcp-scan)
   - Given two cassettes (or a cassette plus a checked-in baseline), compute a stable content hash per tool over name+description+inputSchema and flag drift as a rug-pull finding. The cassette IS the pinned baseline, so no external DB; pure offline diffing over stored MCP handshake bytes.
10. **Unreferenced-interaction lifecycle: warn / reject / delete / auto(CI-aware)** — Graduated policy for stored interactions never hit this run: warn/reject/delete/auto. _(effort M, leverage high)_ [source](https://insta.rs/docs/cli/)
   - After replay/re-record, flag interactions never matched; auto rejects in CI (dead fixtures are a governance smell) and offers local pruning. Pruning is deterministic over the dial log and never contacts the network — it only deletes stale entries, never fabricates.
11. **Prompt-version drift gate: assert the wire prompt matches a pinned content hash** — Fail CI when the canonicalized outbound prompt/system/tool bytes diverge from a pinned hash. _(effort S, leverage high)_ [source](https://langfuse.com/docs/prompts/get-started)
   - Compute the canonical hash of the outbound prompt/system/tool-definition bytes and compare to a pinned expected hash committed alongside; mismatch fails deterministically before anyone re-records. Slots under policy/assert; pure byte comparison, zero egress.
12. **can-i-deploy safety gate: query whether a consumer + its pinned cassettes are compatible before shipping** — One offline deploy/no-deploy exit code aggregating verify/attest/policy across a pinned cassette set. _(effort M, leverage high)_ [source](https://docs.pact.io/getting_started/how_pact_works)
   - Given an app version pinning cassette set S at hashes H, answer offline whether every referenced interaction is present, unexpired, and passing its stored policy pack, emitting a machine-readable matrix. The signed cassettes ARE the offline compatibility matrix; no broker, no network.

## 5. Net-new vs adjacent-inspired

**Genuinely net-new:** Record and govern MCP sampling (server-initiated createMessage) as nested LLM traffic; Distance-ranked replay-miss diagnostics ('did you mean this interaction?'); ANSI terminal-escape injection scanner over recorded model output; Canary-token leak detection: prove a system prompt / secret did not surface in recorded output; import har: ingest an existing HAR capture into a replayable cassette; export har: emit a byte-exact HAR 1.2 file from a recorded cassette

**Adjacent-inspired (borrowed pattern):** cassette review — human-gated accept/reject TUI for a re-recorded delta; Cross-format cassette content assertions (verify-contains / verify-ordering over the Transcript); Rug-pull tripwire: pin tool descriptions/schemas by hash across cassettes; Unreferenced-interaction lifecycle: warn / reject / delete / auto(CI-aware); Prompt-version drift gate: assert the wire prompt matches a pinned content hash; can-i-deploy safety gate: query whether a consumer + its pinned cassettes are compatible before shipping

## 6. What NOT to do / already covered

- **Any re-record mode that silently promotes a changed golden without a human keystroke** — Auto self-healing re-record on drift is explicitly rejected. The review/pending/additive ideas must always require a human accept or explicit --accept batch flag; the moment promotion becomes automatic on mismatch it crosses the rejected line.
- **A stateful/hosted web review dashboard or editor-backend to render the pending-sidecar JSON manifest** — Hosted SaaS / stateful cloud web server / online dashboard is a hard non-goal. The JSON manifest must stay a static file consumed by an external editor extension or CI job; cassette itself only emits bytes, it does not host a server.
- **import otel-genai / HAR import that fabricates response content the capture did not contain** — Built-in LLM fixture generator is rejected. Import must re-frame ONLY verbatim captured messages into a provider wire shape via internal/wireenc; if a field is absent it stays absent — nothing may be model-generated to fill gaps.
- **onUnmatched 'bypass' that falls through to a real upstream network call on replay** — Zero-egress replay is a hard non-goal. The strictness knob's 'bypass' must mean a canned deterministic stub, never a live fetch; any path that touches the network outside opt-in record/branch/watch is forbidden.
- **Generalizing HAR import/export into a generic non-LLM HTTP archive tool** — Not a generic non-LLM VCR — go-vcr/VCR.py/nock own that. The value must stay gated to LLM-shaped provider hosts run through the Transcript decoders; broadening to arbitrary HTTP dissolves the moat and re-treads rejected territory.
- **Toxic-flow / poisoning / near-miss detection backed by an ML classifier or embedding similarity** — No LLM-based classifiers in default flows and embedding/vector-similarity diff are both rejected (nondeterminism + heavy dep). Every detector and distance metric here must be pure vendored pattern tables / string arithmetic so output is byte-reproducible offline.

## 7. Caveats

- Findings rest largely on each project own README/docs — authoritative for capability presence, only suggestive for absence.
- Web search is US-only and time-sensitive (data as of recent); repos move fast.
- Ideas were vetted by LLM agents against the non-goals, not by a human; treat effort/novelty/fit as directional.
- Only the top 50 ideas were clustered in depth; the remainder are listed in the appendix.

## Appendix — also surfaced (lower-ranked)

- **Prompt-set attach: bind an immutable prompt registry to a cassette as governed metadata** (prompt-versioning) — A cassette already IS a byte-exact fixture; add a `cassette attach-prompt` transform that extracts the actual prompt/system text that was sent on the wire (from the recorded request body) and freezes it as a named, content-hashed prompt block inside the cassette YAML's governance section. Because the prompt is derived deterministically from bytes already in the cassette (not authored/generated), it stays offline and deterministic. `inspect`/`explain` can then surface 'this replay was recorded against prompt <name>@<sha256[:8]>', making the cassette a self-describing committable prompt artifact with no external registry. [src](https://mlflow.org/docs/latest/genai/prompt-registry/)
- **Context-scoped redaction confidence surfaced as a coverage-style report** (provenance-supplychain) — Add an explain-mode output to the existing redact/redact-field path (not a new command) that emits, per redacted span, the recognizer name + matched rule + context trigger, deterministically. This turns redaction from a lossy transform into an auditable, reviewable record embedded in the cassette's provenance block, so a reviewer can prove exactly which deterministic rule masked which bytes before the fixture was committed. No live model, no nondeterminism. [src](https://github.com/microsoft/presidio/blob/main/docs/analyzer/index.md)
- **in-toto Statement wrapper so a cassette attestation is portable to any supply-chain verifier** (provenance-supplychain) — Have cassette attest emit its egress/replay attestation as a standards-compliant in-toto Statement: subject = the cassette YAML's content digest, predicateType = a cassette-namespaced URI (e.g. https://cassette.dev/attestation/zero-egress/v1), predicate = the existing attest facts (dial count, decoder versions, redaction rule hashes). This makes cassette's home-grown attestation consumable by any in-toto/cosign verifier in a CI pipeline WITHOUT cassette running a service. Pure serialization of already-computed facts, fully offline, byte-exact. [src](https://github.com/in-toto/attestation/blob/main/spec/v1/statement.md)
- **CDXA-style claim→evidence→requirement conformance attestation for policy runs** (provenance-supplychain) — Let the existing policy/conformance commands emit their pass/fail results as a CDXA document: each policy rule becomes a 'claim' mapped to a named requirement (e.g. 'EU AI Act logging', 'no PII egress'), and the evidence is the concrete cassette artifact + span/hash that satisfied or violated it, including recorded non-conformances. This turns cassette's governance output into an auditor-facing compliance artifact interoperable with GRC tooling, purely as serialization of already-computed policy verdicts. [src](https://cyclonedx.org/capabilities/attestations/)
- **OPA bundle-style signed, versioned policy packs distributed as offline artifacts** (provenance-supplychain) — Let cassette's policy/govern path consume a self-contained, content-hashed 'policy pack' file (the rule set + its version + a digest), and record WHICH policy pack digest was in force when a cassette was checked, embedding that into the attestation. This makes governance verdicts reproducible ('this cassette passed under policy-pack sha256:abc') and lets teams pin/audit their rule set as a first-class artifact — respecting no-SaaS/offline by shipping the pack as a plain file rather than fetching from an OPA bundle server. [src](https://github.com/open-policy-agent/opa)
- **Preview-window filter: fuzzy-find an interaction, preview it live** (cli-dx) — Ship a `--fzf`/pickable list mode on `inspect` that emits a stable one-line-per-interaction index to stdout (idx · method · path · model · first-tokens-of-prompt), designed so `cassette inspect --list / fzf --preview 'cassette inspect {1} --preview'` gives an instant fuzzy picker with a live decoded preview of any interaction. Cassette just needs (a) a machine-stable list format and (b) an `inspect <idx> --preview` that renders one interaction. Deterministic, offline, no bundled fzf dependency — it interops with the tool the user already has, the way delta/bat interop with fzf. [src](https://github.com/junegunn/fzf)
- **Yank the canonical path/selector of any node (record ⇄ replay addressing)** (cli-dx) — Define one canonical, stable selector syntax for addressing any element of a cassette — e.g. `i3.messages[1].content[0]` or `i3.sse[7]` or `i3.tool_calls.get_weather.args.city` — and print it everywhere (in `inspect`, in `diff` hunks, in the TUI as a yankable 'path'). Then let commands that mutate/redact accept that selector (`redact-field`, `assert`, `expect`) so the address you SEE is the address you ACT on. This turns cassette's structured content into first-class navigable coordinates without any new subcommand, and every non-goal holds (deterministic string, offline, no ML). [src](https://github.com/antonmedv/fx)
- **OSC8 clickable hyperlinks from inspect/diff output into files and the TUI** (cli-dx) — Emit OSC8 hyperlinks in `inspect`/`diff`/`doctor` output so an interaction reference is click-to-open: link to the exact byte range in the cassette YAML (open in $EDITOR at line), and — when TTY supports it — link a diff hunk to `open --tui` at that node's selector. Pure ANSI, auto-disabled when piped/non-TTY (same discipline as color), no network, no dependency. Small but high-craft: it stitches the ~60 commands together by making every printed reference actionable. [src](https://github.com/dandavison/delta)
- **Self-contained static viewer BUNDLER for a set of cassettes (range-request friendly)** (blue-sky) — Extend the existing `pack` (which already emits one self-contained offline HTML browser per cassette) with a multi-cassette `pack` mode that bundles a *directory* of cassettes into one static site: a lazily-loaded index over many fixtures plus a range-request layout so a large signed corpus opens instantly offline. - **Targeted review scoping: single-interaction, glob-filter, and keep-pending** (snapshot-testing) — Give the review/diff flow selectors: `--interaction <id>` to review one interaction by its stable id/hash, `--filter <glob>` to scope by request path/model/provider (e.g. only `anthropic` streaming turns), and a resumable pending state so a large multi-turn cassette re-record can be reviewed incrementally across sessions. - **force-refresh metadata without semantic change (canonical re-serialize gated on content-equality)** (snapshot-testing) — A `review --format-only` (or a flag on the existing `canonicalize`) that re-serializes cassettes into the current canonical on-disk format — updated YAML key ordering, codec version bumps, comment/metadata headers — while asserting the DECODED semantic content is byte-identical before and after, refusing to write if any semantic byte changed. - **export openinference: emit an OpenInference-flavored span JSON per interaction** (trace-interop) — A deterministic `export openinference` transform that maps each cassette interaction's decoded Transcript to an OpenInference span object (LLM span with the flattened attribute keys above; MCP tool calls become TOOL spans). - **Numeric / field-level tolerance matchers for replay comparison (custom per-field comparators)** (llmops-awesome) — cassette's canonicalize/redact-field machinery already normalizes noisy fields before byte comparison. - **Deterministic seed/sampling knob for corpus subsetting, borrowed from filterSampleSeed** (prompt-versioning) — Add a deterministic-seed flag to the existing `dataset`/`suite` selection path so that subsetting a large cassette corpus (e.g. 'run 10% of fixtures') is reproducible byte-for-byte across machines and CI given the same seed. This is a structural extension of the existing canonicalize + branch machinery: a cassette can now legitimately encode 'this call has 3 blessed responses' without abandoning determinism (each variant is still byte-exact; only the selection is set-membership).
